211.h: Adamawa State University (ADSU) is a public university owned by the Adamawa State Government. It was established in 2002 under the Adamawa State University Law No. 10 of 2001, with a mission to serve as a centre of learning and development for north-eastern Nigeria. The university has since expanded beyond its original campus, and its Abubakar Barde Campus now hosts the faculties of Agriculture and of Social and Management Sciences.
211.a: ADSU offers bachelor's degrees in faculties that include Sciences, Agriculture, Social Sciences, Arts and Education, along with postgraduate programmes for graduates who want to upgrade or change field. It also runs a one-year foundation programme that prepares students for direct-entry admission to Nigerian universities.
211.c: The main campus is in Mubi, in the northern senatorial district of Adamawa State, close to Nigeria's border with Cameroon.

213.h: Adeleke University is a private, faith-based university founded in 2011 by Dr Adedeji Adeleke through the Springtime Development Foundation. The foundation is a non-profit, non-governmental organisation set up in 1996 to help students from poor families get a good higher education, and it also works in community development, health services and welfare relief. It previously gave scholarships, equipment and infrastructure to students and schools, and it established the university as a larger step towards the same goal. The university is part of the Seventh-day Adventist education system.
213.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
213.c: The campus covers 520 acres in Ede, a historic town in Osun State, south-western Nigeria.

224.h: Arthur Jarvis University (AJU) is a private university founded by Sir Arthur Jarvis Archibong to contribute to education in Cross River State and Nigeria, and named after him. The Federal Government granted it a licence in November 2016, and it was the first private university in Cross River State.
224.a: The Faculty of Natural and Applied Sciences covers the biological, chemical and earth sciences (including geology and applied geophysics), physics, and a computing group with computer science, cyber security, software engineering, data science and artificial intelligence. The Faculty of Humanities, Management and Social Sciences offers accounting, banking and finance, business administration, entrepreneurship, criminology and security studies, marketing, economics, mass communication, political science, public administration, hospitality and tourism, and sociology with peace and conflict resolution.
224.c: It is located in Akpabuyo, near Calabar, the capital of Cross River State.

225.h: Augustine University is a private Catholic university of the Catholic Archdiocese of Lagos. Its visioner was Anthony Cardinal Olubunmi Okogie, Archbishop of Lagos until 2012. The archdiocese has promoted education in its territory since 1973 and earlier founded St Augustine's College of Education in Akoka, Yaba, the first privately owned college of education in Nigeria. The National Universities Commission records the university's establishment in 2015. Its motto, 'Pro Scientia et Moribus', means 'for learning and character'.
225.a: The university aims to provide practical, career-oriented undergraduate and postgraduate programmes that combine personal development with technology, business and management. Its faculties include a Faculty of Science.
225.c: The campus is on Igbonla Road at Ilara-Epe, in Epe local government area of Lagos State.

235.h: Bowen University is a private Christian university in the Baptist tradition, founded by the Nigerian Baptist Convention. The idea is old: a proposal for a Baptist university was presented in 1956 and endorsed in July 1957 by the Baptist Mission of Nigeria and the Nigerian Baptist Convention. The Federal Government approved the university on 17 July 2001, and the National Universities Commission issued its licence. Its first session opened with 506 pioneer students in agriculture, science and science education, and social and management sciences. It is named after Thomas Jefferson Bowen, an American Baptist missionary who worked in Yoruba land in the nineteenth century.
235.a: Bowen aims to offer demanding, morally grounded education at a cost families can manage. Teaching is organised in a modified collegiate system of eight colleges, ranging from computing studies and health sciences, which include medicine, to law, liberal studies and postgraduate studies.
235.c: The university is located at Iwo in Osun State, south-western Nigeria.

237.h: Chrisland University is a private university founded in 2015 by the proprietors of the Chrisland group of schools, and accredited by the National Universities Commission. Its stated mission is to provide a learning environment with a sound moral and intellectual culture that attracts staff from around the world and educates the 'total person'.
237.a: A distinctive feature is that every student graduates with two certificates: a bachelor's degree and a certificate in entrepreneurship training. The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
237.c: It is located in Abeokuta, the capital of Ogun State.

238.h: Christopher University is a private university licensed by the Federal Government on 5 March 2015. It was conceived to run programmes that meet the current and emerging staffing needs of the corporate and public sectors. Its founding programmes in management and the humanities have full accreditation from the National Universities Commission, and it has graduated its pioneer classes.
238.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes with a focus on management, the humanities and related professional fields. It is governed through a Board of Trustees, Governing Council and management, under the oversight of its chancellor.
238.c: It is located in Mowe, Ogun State, on the Lagos-Ibadan expressway corridor, close to Lagos, Nigeria's main commercial hub.

242.h: Crawford University is a private Christian university owned by the Apostolic Faith Mission. It was established in 2005 by Paul Akazue, then leader of the Apostolic Faith work across Africa, who was its proprietor and first chancellor until his death in May 2010. Its stated aim is to be a centre of excellence producing graduates with a well-balanced education.
242.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
242.c: It is located in Igbesa, Ogun State, south-western Nigeria.
